content:
Mateo Alvarez: quick confirm before we cut the next runtime build: are we locked on final metric names + tag keys for SCM? trying to avoid another rename churn.

Omar El-Sayed: yup, we’re ready to lock. Posting what’s in the latest instrumentation patch.

Omar El-Sayed: **Counters**
- `ri.runtime.tokens.prefill_total`
- `ri.runtime.tokens.decode_total`
- `ri.runtime.requests_total`

**Timers (ms)**
- `ri.runtime.latency.prefill_ms`
- `ri.runtime.latency.decode_ms`
- `ri.runtime.latency.e2e_ms`

**Gauges**
- `ri.runtime.batch.batch_size_effective`
- `ri.runtime.cache.kv_hit_rate` (0.0-1.0)
- `ri.runtime.cache.kv_hit_tokens_total` (counter)

All emitted at request-finalization, except `batch_size_effective` which is sampled at admission.

Sofia Ivanova: +1. also we changed naming to avoid “*_seconds” vs “*_ms” confusion. this is consistent w/ other runtime stats.

Logan Wright: tags/labels please. esp anything that’s going to blow up cardinality.

Omar El-Sayed: tag set (final):
- `scm_signal_version=v1`
- `deployment_mode` (hosted|dedicated|private)
- `region`
- `gpu_sku`
- `model_id`
- `model_revision` (optional; only when pinned)
- `quant_profile_id` (optional)
- `route_id` (optional; only if present, otherwise omitted)
- `cache_state` (warm|cold|unknown)

Removed/NOT shipping: `prompt_id`, `tenant_id`, `model_family`. (per Thomas’ cardinality review)

Thomas Baird: :thumbsup: this tag list is acceptable. calling out: `route_id` is the only one that can get spicy; please make sure it’s the canonical route key (normalized) not the raw URL path.

Nadia Rahman: for token metering alignment: `ri.runtime.tokens.*` counts are post-tokenizer, right? (same definition as `metered_input_tokens` / `metered_output_tokens` in the gateway)

Omar El-Sayed: yes. counts are from the same tokenization lib as metering. edge case: tool/function call wrappers add a small fixed preamble; those tokens are included (same as metering).

Jordan Lee: confirm semantics for `batch_size_effective`: is it computed after admission control now? we had the mismatch earlier where it was “requested batch” not “served batch”.

Sofia Ivanova: it’s post-admission. definition we’re using:
`batch_size_effective = number_of_requests_co_batched_for_this_decode_step` (averaged across steps for the request)
we store `batch_size_effective_mean` in-memory and emit once at end.

Mateo Alvarez: great. last thing: during rolling restarts, do we backfill / handle missing tags? cost-model-service was seeing gaps last time.

Omar El-Sayed: behavior during rolling restarts:
- counters reset on process restart (expected)
- first ~30-60s after restart we may emit `cache_state=unknown` until cache warmer finishes
- if `quant_profile_id` not yet loaded from model catalog at startup, we emit **without** the tag (not “unknown”), then it appears once resolved
- we do NOT backfill historical counters; telemetry sees a drop-to-zero which is correct for process-level counters

Logan Wright: this is fine as long as clients don’t treat missing `quant_profile_id` tag as a new value. our aggregation rule is “missing label = bucketed into ‘(none)’ downstream”.

Thomas Baird: please add one note to the PR description: “missing label is omitted (not set to unknown)” — helps w/ query consistency.

Mateo Alvarez: ack. can we also make sure `kv_hit_rate` is emitted as NaN when `cache_state=unknown`? otherwise people assume 0% hit rate.

Sofia Ivanova: good call. currently it’s 0.0 on unknown. we can flip to NaN + emit `cache_state=unknown`. will update.

Omar El-Sayed: done. I’ll patch to emit `kv_hit_rate=NaN` when unknown + add a log line once per minute so we can spot startups that never resolve.

Nadia Rahman: :+1: also note: for very short requests (no decode loop), `batch_size_effective` can be missing. please keep it omitted vs 1.0 to avoid skew.

Omar El-Sayed: yep, omitted when no decode steps.

Mateo Alvarez: ok, locking these. I’ll reply in the SCM thread that runtime metrics/tags are final + restart/backfill behavior documented. thanks all.
